subject: How to write a reproducible example

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: How to write a reproducible example
parts:
Hi all,

Since this comes up a lot, I thought I'd spend a little time writing
up some advice. Any suggestions would be gratefully received, and if
you want to modify the text directly, you can do so at
http://gist.github.com/270442.


# How to write a reproducible example.

You are most likely to get good help with R problem if you provide a
reproducible example. A reproducible example should allow someone else
to recreate your problem just by copying and pasting R code. There
are three things you need to include to make your example
reproducible: required packages, your data and code:

* Packages should be loaded at the top of the script, so it's easy to
see which ones the example needs.

* The easiest way to include data in an email is to use dput() to generate
the R code to recreate it. For example, to recreate the mtcars dataset in
R, I'd perform the following steps:

1. Run `dput(mtcars)` in R
2. Copy the output
3. In my reproducible script, type `mtcars <- ` then paste.

* Spend a little bit of time ensuring that your code is easy for others to
read:

* make sure you've used spaces and your variables are sensible
* use comments to indicate where your problem lies
* do your best to remove everything that is not related to the problem.
The shorter your code is, the easier it is to understand.

Finally, before putting all of your code in an email, consider putting
it on http://gist.github.com/. It will give your code nice syntax
highlighting, and you don't have to worry about anything getting
mangled by the email system.

--
http://had.co.nz/

messages.author: 4e69b94a09c8cf3b
messages.subject: Re: How to write a reproducible example
parts:
In your reproducibility note on git hub you may want to mention what a
"fresh R session" is. Since sessions can be saved and objects can
persist across sessions, ls() and rm() use might be warranted. Maybe
better: start R in a new directory and do the paste test there. This
move has the added benefit of leaving any implicit library loads in
.Rprofile behind. All library/require use should be explicit to the
session for reproducibility.

messages.author: 91408d9f82fba469
messages.subject: Re: How to write a reproducible example
parts:
This is mostly an issue for more inexperienced users. For that purpose I would advise to state that they do not need to use dput for datasets that are part of R or comes with the packages they are using. That might not be clear from the current text.

Kasper
